overall_reason: The job is reading today's agenda: the time column and titles line up, but each event's people line sits as far from its title as from the next event, so the records do not group.

score.reason: T-SQUINT reads the "Today" header first, but T-SKELETON and T-JUDGE-TILE find metadata spaced evenly between records, so the order reads only on a second look.

findings.where: event records, x 488 to 663, y 66 to 218, 1440px
findings.evidence: dom-1440.json: "Design review" ends at y=84 and "Maya and Jon" starts at y=94 (10px gap). "Maya and Jon" ends at y=110 and the next title "Customer call" starts at y=120 (also 10px). The 11:00 and 2:00 records repeat the same spacing. Draft LAY-284 asks for a title closer to its metadata than to the next record.
findings.before: Equal 10px gaps above and below each metadata line.
findings.after: Set each title and its metadata as one item with a 2 to 4px gap, and open the gap between records.
findings.why: With even gaps, "Maya and Jon" reads as belonging to either neighbouring event.

strengths: Times sit on their own track at x=413 and titles at x=488, so the agenda has two clean columns.
The "Today" header (14px/550) with the date on the right gives the card one title.
